newsitem.title: USA: Harleys are most stolen motorcycles proportionally.
newsitem.headline: Harleys are most stolen motorcycles proportionally.

text.p: More Harley-Davidsons are stolen in proportion to total numbers owned than any other motorcycles in the United States, said a study released Wednesday by an insurance claims analysis firm.

CCC Information Services, based here, said Harleys accounted for 27 percent of all U.S. motorcycle thefts last year, although the Milwaukee-made machines accounted for only 14 percent of motorcycles on U.S. roads in the same period.

CCC said Hondas comprised 30 percent of U.S. bikes on the road in 1995 and accounted for 28 percent of thefts; Suzukis for 19 percent and 17 percent of thefts; Kawasakis for 18 percent and 15 percent of thefts; Yamahas for 17 percent and 11 percent of thefts.
There were 9,224 motorcycle thefts in the United States in 1995, up 46 percent since 1992, said the National Insurance Crime Bureau in a separate study released this summer.
CCC said its study was requested by the FBI and the National Association of Independent Insurers after they questioned some of the findings of the July NICB study.
CCC said its study was based on an analysis of motorcycle insurance claims and total loss valuations submitted to insurers through CCC Information Services.
